[LFST.7.3.6] When consuming one input event (a host fact assert or retract,
or an adapter event) triggers downstream truth-maintenance effects
(justification withdrawal → logical-fact retract, or re-justification → assert),
the engine must assign the input event's own stream record a `seq` before the
records of the effects it causes ([RFCS.6.7]). An engine withdrawal is ordered
the same way, before the withdrawals it cascades into ([RFCS.7a.4]). For these
a reader never observes a cascade `fact_retract`/`fact_assert` earlier in `seq`
than the event that caused it: the triggering event is consumed before its
consequences are processed, the causal reading of [LFST.7.3.1] (`seq` =
consumption order). It is the event-trace corollary of the justification-linkage
principle ([LLOG.15]).

A rule's assert is not ordered so. Each RHS action is propagated before it is
recorded, so a retraction an `emit` causes is recorded ahead of
that action ([RARC.5.6.8]).
